changelog:
What you'll see with this update:
• Update reliability: updates now come from a version-pinned source, so an update can never half-install again (a unit could previously show the new version while still running old settings, and then refuse to re-apply).
• 'Config Check' row: the result no longer carries a trailing number (it was an internal timestamp).
• The settings row 'Boots' is now 'Warnings' (in future it can carry alerts other than booting, too): the row reads 'Repeated restarts' instead of the cryptic 'RESTART_STORM', with a plain-English message ('The unit restarted N times in the last 24h... please contact Cytech Support.'). The guard itself is unchanged: it flags 5+ restarts in 24h so Cytech can help.
If your unit is coming from an older version, this update also includes:
• Config self-healing: if the main settings file is ever damaged, the unit repairs it from the last known-good copy (at boot, or within 4 hours while running) and tells you (popup + email).
• A 'Config Check' row in the settings screen, refreshed right after every restart and every 4 hours.
• A clean alert-email setup: your address field is 'My Email for Alerts'; Register shows its result on screen; alerts always reach Cytech Support too, with your address copied automatically.
details: v42f is v42e plus one change: the update notice itself. The 'changelog' field is now a short owner-facing summary; the full technical history is this 'details' field, which only goes into the update log (cytech_update.sh echoes it as 'Update details'). This release is the same as v42e: (1) raw.githubusercontent.com serves each URL from a CDN with max-age=300, keyed by the URL itself (a query string does NOT create a separate entry -- verified 2026-09-04), so a device downloading right after a release could be served the PREVIOUS version's file with no error, then write the new version label -- silently half-updated, and permanently unable to re-apply ('the units can never pull the real package, because the checker considers it up to date'). v42c hit exactly that on the bench unit. THE FIX: every release is git-tagged with its version (42f) and files are downloaded from the tag URL -- a URL no device has ever fetched, so it can never be served from cache. The manifest itself stays on the branch URL (stale reads there are harmless: 'up to date' for at most 5 minutes, then the next check is fresh). (2) cytech_integrity_check.py writes the status word only ('ok'), not 'ok <epoch>' -- the epoch leaked onto the Config Check dashboard row as an unexplained number. (3) The boot guard state RESTART_STORM became REPEATED_RESTARTS with plain-English messages ('Repeated restarts detected' popup/email; message 'The unit restarted N times in the last 24h (first at HH:MM:SS local). Repeated restarts usually mean a problem -- please contact Cytech Support.'). Automation id cytech_alert_boot_storm is unchanged. (3b) The sensor 'Cytech Boot Status' is renamed 'Cytech Warning' -- the row is expected to carry other warnings besides boot/restart ones -- and its unique_id is bumped to cytech_warning_result_sensor on purpose: the entity registry pins an entity_id at first registration, so a name change alone would NOT move the id (the v42b lesson). A bumped unique_id re-registers every unit fresh as sensor.cytech_warning; units that already ran v35+ keep the orphaned sensor.cytech_boot_status (unreferenced, harmless, same pattern as the v42a orphan). The on-disk result file (/config/.cytech_boot_result) and the dashboard row's message attribute are unchanged. Also note: .cytech_secrets.example now warns not to pin CYTECH_MANIFEST_URL to a tag (the tag changes every release). Release history for jumpers: v42d was the re-release attempted for the v42c situation and was itself caught by the stale CDN while being offered (it took the bench unit 4 hours, from 10:24 push to 11:46 'Update Now', for the offer to show; the apply then succeeded: core restarted 11:47:45, real 42c bytes, start-triggered integrity check wrote the status 33 s after start); it is superseded. v42c made the Config Check row stop showing 'unknown' for up to 4 hours after an update restart -- the runtime integrity check now also runs right after every core start (boot AND update restarts), so the row shows its real result (ok / restored / error) within minutes, and before the first run ever it reads 'waiting' instead of HA's error-lookalike 'unknown'. v42b fixed the row showing 'Entity not found' because Home Assistant pins an entity_id in its entity registry the first time a unique_id is seen -- renaming a sensor does not move a registered entity_id, so the sensor's unique_id was changed and every unit registers fresh as sensor.cytech_integrity_status (the id the row references). v42a was the earlier rename-only attempt that couldn't heal already-registered units. Units coming from v39 or older also get v42/v41/v40 below. v42 makes a corrupted configuration.yaml self-healing, and not just at boot: the system keeps a rolling known-good snapshot of configuration.yaml (refreshed after every clean check -- at boot and every 4 hours while running), and if the live file is ever found corrupt it is replaced by the snapshot with the broken copy saved as configuration.yaml.corrupt.<timestamp>, HA restarts (runtime corruption is repaired the same day it happens, before the next update's restart could land the system in HA recovery mode), and the integrity alert says so. Two safety properties: the snapshot is only refreshed after the configuration actually parsed clean, so a corrupted state can never be snapshotted as 'good'; and no restore happens unless the snapshot itself parses, so there is no restore loop. Integrity alerts are now also emailed (support@cytech.biz always, plus the owner's registered address per the v41 rule), and the System Health dashboard shows a Config Check row with the last running check result. For v39 or older, v42f also carries v40 and v41: the owner's address field is 'My Email for Alerts', a Register press always reports its status on screen (empty field: 'Enter your email first, then press Register.'), a successful Register sends ONE confirmation mail To: the owner Cc: support@cytech.biz, alerts ALWAYS go to support@cytech.biz with the owner's registered address copied automatically (no Cytech/Me/Both selector), and units with mail configured but no owner registered yet show a small non-blocking hint. Nothing is lost if the owner never registers: support@cytech.biz always receives every alert.
